title: Twenty-Five Twenty-One
hook: How does Twenty-Five Twenty-One end? The breakup nobody wanted, the diary device, and why Hee-do and Yi-jin do not stay together, explained.

sections.heading: Where the finale leaves them
sections.body: The final stretch finds fencer Na Hee-do at the height of her career and reporter Baek Yi-jin chasing a foothold in journalism. Their teenage romance, born in the IMF crisis years, has matured, but the distance between an athlete in Korea and a reporter increasingly stationed abroad keeps pulling at the seams. The whole story is framed from 2021, where Hee-do's daughter Kim Min-chae, having quit ballet, discovers her mother's old diary at her grandmother's house and begins reading the chronicle of 1998 onward, so the audience always knows the ending is being recalled, not lived forward.

sections.heading: September 11 and the slow breakup
sections.body: The key turn is not a villain or a betrayal but circumstance. Yi-jin is sent to cover the September 11 attacks in New York and pursues a permanent posting there. The grind of his career leaves Hee-do increasingly alone, and the relationship erodes under the weight of his absence. Their final argument turns cruel, both of them hurling hateful words they instantly regret. The breakup is mutual and devastating precisely because no one is at fault. The show insists that two people can love each other completely and still be pulled apart by the lives they are building.

sections.heading: What the final scene means
sections.body: The diary device pays off twenty years later. Hee-do recovers the journal she kept during their separation, filled with the words she wished she had said in that last fight. Yi-jin, it turns out, had also written his own unspoken feelings into the same pages. The reveal reframes the breakup not as a failure of love but as a failure of timing and presence. The closing beat answers the question the whole series asks about first love. When prompted for his first love as a security answer, Yi-jin types the name Na Hee-do, confirming what he never stopped feeling.

sections.heading: Why the ending lands the way it does
sections.body: The thematic payoff is that first love can be formative without being forever. In the epilogue both reach the success they chased, Yi-jin as a news anchor and Hee-do winning further gold medals before retiring in 2009. The framing daughter, Min-chae, draws strength from her mother's youth and returns to her own dreams. The drama refuses the reunion fans wanted because its real subject is how the people who shaped us stay with us even after they leave. Their glory days remain golden precisely because they ended, preserved rather than worn down.

final_image: Yi-jin, asked for his first love as a password security answer, types the name Na Hee-do, the screen confirming the feeling the series spent eighteen years tracing.

lingering_questions.q: Do Hee-do and Yi-jin end up together in Twenty-Five Twenty-One?
lingering_questions.a: No. They break up in the finale, worn down by Yi-jin's career abroad and the distance it creates. The epilogue shows them successful but apart, with Yi-jin still naming Hee-do as his first love.

lingering_questions.q: Why do Na Hee-do and Baek Yi-jin break up?
lingering_questions.a: Circumstance rather than any betrayal. Yi-jin's reporting career, including covering the September 11 attacks, takes him abroad and leaves Hee-do alone, eroding the relationship until a painful final argument ends it.
